# Chakra UI adapter

**Status:** Experimental
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0
**Implementation reviewed:** Chakra UI 3.37.0 on 2026-09-11

This adapter exposes reviewed GOV.UK values through a reset-free Chakra UI 3 system for service-owned extensions. It does not recreate GOV.UK components, make Chakra recipes markup-compatible, or treat a Chakra theme as evidence of GOV.UK conformance.

## Compatibility level

- `guidance`
- `token`
- `markup`
- `behaviour-tested`

These levels describe this adapter's bounded evidence. They do not mean that Chakra UI itself supplies GOV.UK components, that a service is accessible, or that a theme makes an implementation conformant.

## Scope and requirements

- Use GOV.UK Frontend CSS, JavaScript and official component markup for GOV.UK components. Chakra primitives, style props, recipes and snippets are for clearly service-owned extensions, not substitutes for `govuk-*` classes, component DOM or progressive enhancement.
- Treat the generated `govuk-system.mjs` as a reviewed token bridge. Token availability does not include GOV.UK usage rules, semantics, responsive component behaviour, accessibility or permission to use identity assets.
- Render native controls, validation, disclosure content and essential actions in the initial HTML. Server-render and hydrate Chakra where the host supports it, but keep the journey usable if Chakra styles or client JavaScript do not run.
- Keep Chakra-managed state outside GOV.UK Frontend-enhanced subtrees. After `initAll`, do not ask React or Chakra to reconcile descendants that GOV.UK Frontend has mutated.
- Confirm separately that the service may use GDS Transport, the GOV.UK crown and other protected identity assets. This bridge deliberately maps no font family and includes no identity artwork.

## Installation and build order

- Install the reviewed implementation with `npm install --save-dev --save-exact @chakra-ui/react@3.37.0 @emotion/react@11.14.0`. Chakra UI 3 requires Node 20 or newer and declares React and React DOM 18 or newer as peers; use versions supported by the host application. The fixture uses the repository's pinned React 19.3.0 and React DOM 19.3.0.
- Import `govuk-system.mjs` into a client-capable React boundary and pass it to `<ChakraProvider value={govukChakraSystem}>`. A colour-mode provider is optional and is intentionally omitted from this fixed GOV.UK light presentation.
- Load the canonical `design/govuk/tokens/govuk.css`, then any narrowly scoped service fallback CSS, and keep GOV.UK Frontend CSS authoritative for `govuk-*` components. Copy GOV.UK Frontend fonts, images and JavaScript to stable application asset URLs rather than hotlinking them.
- Run Chakra type generation against the generated system module if the host uses strict TypeScript token checking. Regenerate types whenever the reviewed bridge changes and do not hand-edit generated token output.

## Preflight and cascade

- Create the bridge from Chakra's `defaultBaseConfig`, set `preflight: false`, keep `globalCss` empty and set `disableLayers: true`. This retains supported style-property machinery without applying Chakra's element reset or application-wide base styles over GOV.UK Frontend, and avoids emitting empty layer declarations around the token variables.
- Do not switch the bridge to `defaultConfig` or enable a scoped reset without reviewing every resulting token, recipe, global rule and cascade interaction. Chakra's default design language is not the GOV.UK Design System.
- Chakra can use cascade layers for resets, base rules, tokens and recipes, but this bounded bridge disables them because it has no reset, global CSS or recipes. Layer order alone is not a component-compatibility guarantee: keep Chakra style props off the internal DOM of official GOV.UK components and never use `!important` to force an override.
- Keep the service-owned fallback selector narrow and load it without hiding or disabling content. It may preserve basic layout and colour when Emotion or client JavaScript is unavailable, but it must not style internal `govuk-*` component classes.

## Token mapping

- The generated ES module creates a namespaced Chakra system with `cssVarsPrefix: "govuk-chakra"`. Reviewed values reference canonical `--govuk-*` custom properties so the portable GOV.UK token file remains the value source.
- Functional colours use names such as `govuk-brand`, `govuk-text`, `govuk-surface`, `govuk-surface-border`, `govuk-focus`, `govuk-error` and `govuk-success`. Palette values remain under a `govuk-` prefix; unprefixed Chakra colours are not GOV.UK values.
- Static spacing uses values such as `govuk-4`; responsive spacing uses names such as `govuk-responsive-6` and follows the canonical custom property at the 641px GOV.UK tablet breakpoint. `govuk-page` exposes the reviewed maximum page width.
- The system exposes `govuk-mobile`, `govuk-tablet` and `govuk-desktop` breakpoints plus reviewed typography sizes, line heights and regular and bold weights. It deliberately omits a font-family token.
- Use complete token names in Chakra style props and run Chakra type generation in typed projects. Do not add local aliases that obscure whether a value came from GOV.UK, Chakra defaults or the service's own design decisions.

## Official components and behaviour

- Translate official component HTML to JSX mechanically, including elements, `className`, `htmlFor`, IDs, `data-module` and ARIA relationships. Chakra components that render similar-looking controls are neither DOM nor behaviour compatible with GOV.UK Frontend.
- Use Chakra `Box` and other primitives only for service-owned wrappers whose ownership is explicit in code. Keep GOV.UK components as native JSX elements with their complete `govuk-*` class contract.
- Hydrate the server-rendered tree before dynamically importing and initialising GOV.UK Frontend. Initialise each stable scope once, keep enhanced descendants passive, and replace a whole enhancement boundary rather than reconciling inside it.
- Keep Accordion and Tabs content visible in initial HTML. Test mouse, keyboard, focus, validation, hydration diagnostics and JavaScript-disabled behaviour with the assembled GOV.UK, Chakra and fallback styles.

## Browser support

- Use the intersection of the browser support policies for the host React version, Chakra UI, Emotion and GOV.UK Frontend. Chakra's Node 20 minimum is a build and server-runtime requirement, not a statement of browser support.
- GOV.UK Frontend's graded browser model still governs official components. Do not make an essential task depend on Chakra-generated presentation in a browser the service must support unless that exact assembled application has been tested.
- Because the initial HTML contains native controls and visible disclosure content, a missing Chakra client bundle must not block the journey. Keep a small static fallback only where service-owned layout or meaning would otherwise be lost.
- Re-check framework, runtime and browser requirements when upgrading any pinned dependency. A passing Chakra theme migration does not prove that GOV.UK Frontend hydration, cascade or accessibility contracts remain intact.

## Build example

Create a reset-free system from the base Chakra configuration and reference the canonical GOV.UK custom properties from namespaced tokens:

```js
import { createSystem, defaultBaseConfig, defineConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react'

const config = defineConfig({
  cssVarsPrefix: 'govuk-chakra',
  disableLayers: true,
  preflight: false,
  globalCss: {},
  theme: {
    breakpoints: {
      'govuk-mobile': '320px',
      'govuk-tablet': '641px',
      'govuk-desktop': '769px'
    },
    tokens: {
      colors: {
        'govuk-text': { value: 'var(--govuk-color-text)' },
        'govuk-surface': { value: 'var(--govuk-color-surface-background)' },
        'govuk-surface-border': { value: 'var(--govuk-color-surface-border)' }
      },
      spacing: {
        'govuk-responsive-6': { value: 'var(--govuk-spacing-responsive-6)' }
      },
      sizes: {
        'govuk-page': { value: 'var(--govuk-layout-page-width)' }
      }
    }
  }
})

export const govukChakraSystem = createSystem(defaultBaseConfig, config)
```

Use Chakra style props on an explicitly service-owned wrapper while official component elements retain their complete GOV.UK contract:

```jsx
<ChakraProvider value={govukChakraSystem}>
  <Box
    as="section"
    data-chakra-service-wrapper
    bg="govuk-surface"
    color="govuk-text"
    p="govuk-responsive-6"
    maxW="govuk-page"
  >
    <h2 className="govuk-heading-m">Application details</h2>
    <button className="govuk-button" data-module="govuk-button" type="submit">
      Save and continue
    </button>
  </Box>
</ChakraProvider>
```

## Reference fixture

The development SSR and hydration fixture starts with `npm run fixture:serve:chakra` and renders `fixtures/chakra/app.mjs`. It uses Chakra UI 3.37.0 and Emotion 11.14.0 for one service-owned token surface, while Button, Text input and Accordion retain official GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 markup, CSS and behaviour. The fixture includes a static CSS fallback, renders essential content on the server and is test evidence rather than package payload or a starter application. Chakra UI 3 requires Node 20 or newer.
